defects_found: The chrome overflowed the page at 320 px with a long workspace name: .collab-switcher and .collab-account are flex items and default to min-width auto, so the context name could not shrink and its ellipsis never applied. CF-P7-012 could not see it because it qualified the switcher on its own, with no flex parent to refuse; the composed chrome is the only place it appears.

blocked_on.owner_action: Push a commit carrying the CF-P7-017 fix (functions/_lib/identity/environment.ts, functions/_lib/api-shell.mjs) and trigger a new codex-cf-p3-preview build -- Cloudflare Pages binds code at build time, so the existing deployment cannot show it -- then drive the signed-in journeys, which no agent can do because obtaining an OAuth session means entering credentials at github.com.
blocked_on.reason: Re-measured 2026-07-27. The originally recorded blocker -- COLLABORATION_ENABLED not set for the Preview environment -- was cleared by the owner and changed nothing on the wire. The second, deeper blocker was in the code: functions/_lib/api-shell.mjs computed hasReviewedDisabledState and returned the identical 503 on both branches, while functions/_lib/identity/environment.ts gated the three real dispatch doors on a flag read with the opposite polarity to its name. That was CF-P7-017, and it is now PASS: D-P7-02 (decision-log.md) decided environment.ts was the bug, the polarity is corrected, and api-shell.mjs's dead branch is removed, verified against the local Workers-runtime harness (CF-EV-P7-OPS-006). Nothing about that fix has been observed on a deployment, because no agent pushed a commit or triggered a new Preview build -- Cloudflare Pages binds code at build time, so the deployment recorded below still reflects the pre-fix behaviour. A third reason survives the fix entirely: the journeys to be qualified are signed-in journeys and no OAuth session is available to an agent, so qualifying this story remains owner-driven regardless of the deployment.
blocked_on.owner_action_taken_and_insufficient: COLLABORATION_ENABLED='true' was set for the Pages Preview environment (D-P7-01) and the dispatch bug was fixed in the working tree (CF-P7-017, D-P7-02). Both necessary. Neither sufficient without a new deployment and a signed-in session.
blocked_on.dispatch_bug_status: FIXED in the working tree by CF-P7-017; not yet observed on any deployment.

journeys_not_completable_in_this_build.missing: an unlock secret to protect the device key
journeys_not_completable_in_this_build.reason: DeviceKeyLifecycle.enroll takes an unlock secret, and the passphrase surface that would collect one is not among the twelve CF-P7-001 froze. Adding it is a contract change under its own story, not an implementation detail of this one.

journeys_not_completable_in_this_build.missing: a client-side workspace-DEK sealer, and an active device to seal to
journeys_not_completable_in_this_build.reason: runCreateWorkspace needs keys.sealCreatorEnvelope, which exists nowhere in the browser: Phase 5 shipped the device key pair and the server-side envelope services, and Phase 6 drove the sealing by hand. Writing one here would be a new cryptographic primitive, which the Phase 7 governing principle forbids. The surface states the nearer half of the reason itself -- there is no active device -- and holds its submit control disabled rather than failing on press.

journeys_not_completable_in_this_build.missing: an active device to bind the membership to
journeys_not_completable_in_this_build.reason: InvitationAcceptRequest carries a device id, and device registration is unavailable for the reason above. The review half is composed and reads live: the token is taken from the fragment, the address bar is cleared by replacement, and the invitation is described. Only the final accept is held, with the surface stating why.

A conflict is raised by a document mutation, and no document surface exists in the frozen Phase 7 inventory -- the handoff scoped the document experience but CF-P7-001 froze twelve surfaces without one. The dialog composes and renders its own no-conflict state; it cannot be reached by a user in this build.

journeys_not_completable_in_this_build.missing: an actual signed-in GitHub session, which no agent may obtain
journeys_not_completable_in_this_build.reason: CF-P7-013's follow-up work closed the original gap: js/collaboration/api-client.js now carries beginSignIn(), the one CSRF-exempt mutation the frozen server contract accepts before a session exists, and js/collaboration/entry.js wires the rendered control to it -- verified structurally (simulated click, refusal, and double-click cases) and against the real Preview deployment's POST /api/v1/oauth/github/transactions (201, a valid authorizationUrl, 3/3 attempts). What remains is not a code gap: the deployment measured below (4c5d7c8a) predates both this fix and CF-P7-017's dispatch fix, and completing the journey end to end requires entering GitHub credentials at github.com, which no agent may do regardless of what the code does.

declared_limits.sync_reason: Saving, Offline, and Conflict are all derived from outbox entries for an open document, and there is no document surface in the frozen inventory to create one. Saved and Access removed do not need one: Saved is the empty queue, and Access removed is reached from a real workspace-scoped denial followed by a membership re-check, which this build performs.
